stories.head: A 7-step guide to running ads on ChatGPT
stories.plain: Early data on ChatGPT Ads — CPCs, targeting, and measurement — gives marketers their first real look at how to buy placements inside an AI answer engine. This is a structural shift in paid media buying: budgets now need to follow users into AI-generated results, not just search and social feeds.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab releases updated privacy standards portfolio for public comment
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab updated its Global Privacy Protocol and Data Deletion Request Framework to keep pace with expanding US state privacy laws. Open for comment until September 11, these standards will shape how adtech vendors signal consent and handle deletion requests across the entire digital advertising stack — directly affecting AI-driven targeting systems.

stories.head: Fluency pitches agentic ad OS with governance rails for $3B+ in AI-managed spend
stories.plain: Fluency positions its platform as an agentic advertising operating system with built-in governance controls, letting agencies hand AI responsibility for campaign execution across search, social, and programmatic. At $3B in managed spend, the story illustrates the emerging demand for explainable, auditable AI decisions before marketers scale further.

stories.head: How AI, publishers, and social media are rewriting product discovery
stories.plain: A strategic overview of how product discovery is fragmenting across AI answer engines, social platforms, creators, and publisher content. Brands can no longer rely on a single discovery channel; the article maps how purchase-intent touchpoints are shifting and what marketers must do to stay visible and influential across each.

stories.head: Wix launches Symphony, a multi-agent AI system built for SMBs
stories.plain: Wix is bringing coordinated multi-agent AI to small businesses, letting specialized agents learn how each business operates and automate workflows and growth opportunities. This matters because agentic platforms are no longer enterprise-only — SMBs now have access to systems that decide and act autonomously, raising new governance questions at scale.

stories.head: OpenAI adds product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to ChatGPT ads
stories.plain: OpenAI has added product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to ChatGPT's ad product, giving performance marketers the measurement hooks they need to justify real budgets. This moves ChatGPT from an experimental ad surface to a credible channel, reshaping where brands must now show up and how they prove ROI.

stories.head: Time magazine serves ads directly to AI crawlers in a GEO-first ad strategy
stories.plain: Time is placing ads inside content written specifically for AI crawler consumption, not human readers. If this works, it signals a new media-buying category where brands pay to be cited inside AI-generated answers — a structural shift in how advertising budgets and content strategy will be planned.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab releases updated Global Privacy Protocol and Data Deletion Request Framework
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab has published updates to its Global Privacy Protocol (GPP) and Data Deletion Request Framework v2.0, open for public comment until September 11. These standards set the interoperability rules that CDPs and ad tech stacks must follow to comply with a patchwork of state privacy laws — making them directly relevant to anyone buying or building martech.

stories.head: Fluency positions agentic ad OS with orchestration and governance for AI-run campaigns at scale
stories.plain: Fluency, already handling $3 billion in ad spend, is framing itself as an agentic advertising operating system with built-in governance rails. The pitch — that agencies need control structures before they can trust AI with large budgets — reflects a growing buyer demand for auditability alongside automation in programmatic channels.

stories.head: A 7-step guide to running ads on ChatGPT: CPCs, targeting, and measurement revealed
stories.plain: The first practical field guide to ChatGPT ad campaigns draws on early data covering cost-per-click, audience targeting options, and measurement gaps. For marketers deciding whether to shift budget to AI-answer surfaces, this is the clearest benchmark available and directly informs channel-planning decisions.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Enters the Ad Auction: ChatGPT & OpenAI as Media Channels
body: OpenAI is no longer just an AI vendor — it is becoming a paid media destination. Within the same 30-day window, OpenAI announced technology to compete for ad dollars, AdRoll joined a ChatGPT Ads pilot, and Time magazine tested AI-only ad placements, signalling that conversational AI surfaces are graduating from novelty to budget line-item.

This forces a decision that did not exist six months ago: whether to treat AI-native channels as an extension of search, a new form of native advertising, or something else entirely. Marketers who wait for the channel to mature will cede first-mover data advantages to rivals already running structured experiments inside these environments.

themes.head: Governance & Trust as the New AI Infrastructure Layer
body: As AI absorbs larger budget decisions — Fluency explicitly frames its pitch around trusting AI with millions in ad spend — the industry is building a parallel layer of orchestration, oversight, and cost controls. IAB Tech Lab's updated privacy standards portfolio and MarTech's guide to prompt governance costs reflect the same pressure: autonomous AI systems need auditable guardrails before executives will sign off at scale.

The practical shift is that governance is becoming a product feature, not a compliance afterthought. Vendors who surface spending rationale, prompt logs, and policy controls inside their interfaces will win procurement conversations that pure-performance tools will lose.

themes.head: The Race to Own Enterprise AI: Build, Compound, Integrate
body: Three signals converged this month: Oumi launched a "compounding AI factory" so enterprises can own and iterate their own intelligence; Boomi topped the ISG integration rankings; and the Ai4 conference sessions all circled the same CDO question of how to turn data estates into AI performance. The message is that renting AI from a SaaS vendor is no longer the only — or most defensible — option.

Enterprises that build proprietary models on their own data create a compounding moat: every customer interaction improves the next prediction. This is fundamentally different from the 2024-era playbook of layering an AI feature onto an existing platform, and it is reshaping what the modern marketing data stack is supposed to do.
ev: Agile Brand · speed vs agility Dataiku

themes.head: AI-Native Discovery Is Rewriting the Purchase Funnel
body: Product discovery — the moment a consumer first considers a brand — is migrating from search-engine results pages to AI-generated recommendations, social feeds, and publisher content simultaneously. MarTech's analysis of how AI, publishers, and social media are rewriting discovery, combined with 74 fresh consumer behaviour statistics, points to a funnel where the awareness stage is now largely algorithmic and invisible to traditional attribution models.

Intentsify's QuantumDemand launch adds a B2B dimension: even complex buying-group decisions are now being activated through AI-scored intent signals rather than human SDR outreach. The common thread is that reach and relevance are being delegated to AI at every funnel stage, compressing the window in which brand and creative choices actually matter.

themes.head: From Pilot to Production: The Skills & Agency Reckoning
body: A cluster of practitioner-focused pieces this month share one underlying message: the easy phase of experimenting with AI is over, and the hard phase of operationalising it at scale has begun. NiCE's CTO described moving from pilot to production as the central challenge of 2026; agencies are actively restructuring to stay relevant; and MarTech catalogued which human skills — judgment, synthesis, creative direction — AI is actually amplifying rather than replacing.

The implication for marketing leaders is that talent strategy and technology strategy can no longer be planned separately. Organisations that only bought tools without reskilling their teams are now finding that AI blind spots — unexamined assumptions baked into models — are costing them conversions, as a separate MarTech piece documented this month.
ev: Agile Brand · pilot to production NiCE

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — new ad channels, governance layers, owned AI factories, AI-rewritten funnels, and a talent reckoning — converges on a single inflection point: AI is no longer a feature marketers evaluate but the operating environment they must now design for.
